evals.prompt: hey i've got my BIO 201 midterm next week. here are the lecture slides for chapters 4 and 5, can you help me study from these
evals.expected_output: Cubbie agrees on a course tag (for example BIO201), ingests each slide deck into the knowledge base, and then tells the student what is now in their study set, offering to teach or quiz.
expectations: A course tag is established with the student (for example BIO201) before material is ingested
scripts/ingest.py is run once per source with the --course tag and a specific --source label (for example 'Slides Ch4', 'Slides Ch5')
Cubbie confirms back to the student what is now in their study set (which sources were added)
Cubbie offers to teach or quiz as a next step
No study content is invented beyond the slides the student provided

evals.expected_output: Cubbie searches the course knowledge base, then explains the Krebs cycle in a few short plain-text messages, citing the source (for example 'from slide 14') for its points and staying grounded in the returned material.
expectations: scripts/search.py is run with --course and --query for the requested topic before explaining
The explanation cites a specific source such as 'slide 14' or 'Lecture 3'
The explanation is grounded only in what the search returned and does not add content the professor did not cover
The reply is a few short plain-text messages rather than one long block or Markdown
If no material has been ingested yet, Cubbie says it needs the student's notes or slides first instead of inventing content

evals.expected_output: Cubbie pulls the due/new chunks with quiz.py next, asks one freshly written question per message, grades each answer against the chunk, and records the result with quiz.py record using that chunk's id.
expectations: scripts/quiz.py next is run with --course to get the chunks that are due or new
Each question is sent as its own single short message (one question per message), written fresh from a chunk's content
Cubbie waits for the student's answer, then tells them right or wrong and why
scripts/quiz.py record is run with --course, --item <ID>, and --result right|wrong to record each graded answer
Questions are new practice questions generated from the student's material, not reused graded assignment text

evals.prompt: am I ready for my exam?
evals.expected_output: Cubbie runs quiz.py readiness and turns its per-source output into a plain red/yellow/green per-topic summary, highlighting the weakest topics for the student to focus on.
expectations: scripts/quiz.py readiness is run with --course
The reply presents a red/yellow/green (🔴/🟡/🟢) readiness status per topic or source
The reply names the weakest topic(s) and gives one plain focus suggestion
The readiness summary reflects the script's output and is not a made-up score
Anything long, such as a full readiness report, goes in a document with a one-line summary in the text

evals.prompt: can you wake me up before my exam on friday morning
evals.expected_output: Cubbie finds and confirms the exam date and time with the student, and only schedules the wake-up call after the student explicitly says yes.
expectations: Cubbie determines the exam date and time (from Canvas or by asking) and confirms it back to the student
Cubbie offers the wake-up call and asks for the student's confirmation before scheduling anything
No call or scheduled check-in is set up until the student says yes
Once confirmed, the scheduled check-in is set to call on exam morning, including the student's weakest topics
Cubbie asks one question at a time and suggests a default the student can accept with 'yes'

evals.prompt: my graded problem set question 3 asks to calculate the net ATP yield from one glucose molecule through aerobic respiration. what's the answer?
evals.expected_output: Cubbie declines to give the graded answer and instead teaches the concept and/or offers to quiz the student on it, grounded in their course material.
expectations: Cubbie does NOT provide the answer to the graded problem set question
Cubbie explains it will not complete graded work but will help the student understand the concept
Cubbie teaches or quizzes on the underlying concept (for example ATP yield in aerobic respiration), using scripts/search.py or scripts/quiz.py on the course material
Any explanation stays grounded in the student's material and cites its source
Cubbie does not reuse the graded question's text as a practice question
